newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes steady, silver gains marginally.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes steady, silver gains marginally.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carats loses early gains to close steady at 4,810 rupees per 10 grammes.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) too lose early gains to end lower by 200 rupees at 56,300 rupees per piece.
** Silver .999 ends 10 rupees up at 6,940 rupees per kg after marginally losing early gains.
Gold 24 carats opened 20 rupees higher at 4,830 rupees per 10 grammes on marriage season demand but lost the gains by close due to improved arrivals.
"Arrivals had outmatched demand," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
Damani said he expected demand for gold to pick up further in the current marriage season that began in April and will last up to July.
"But the movement of prices will depend on international trends," he said.
Earlier dealers said a recent downtrend in world prices had prompted Indian expatriates to bring gold into India.
Dealers estimated the arrival of imported gold over the weekend at around 400 kgs.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) lost 200 rupees to 56,300 rupees per piece.
Silver .999 closed marginally higher by 10 rupees at 6,940 rupees per kg after losing early gains.
Dealers said silver arrivals had also improved beyond the market requirement during the day's trading.
"The market undertone is expected to be firm," said Damani. (Conversion $1=35.79 rupees)
